description_en: Rumal Stone Fountain in Lamji, built between 14th and 16th centuries, is accessible via a motorable path that departs from the Dullu's central area. The Fountain stands on the north side of the path, 100 meters east of the Lamjī Pañcadevala (DLK0320) and faces north. It has a central panel carved with pilasters and a horizontal frieze ofāmalakamotifs, as do most Karnali monuments of this type. Water is dispensed through a stylized makara head. Each side of the central panel has a small platform. On both sides of the fountain, a larger platform made of stone and cement has been added. The central panel has been partially dismantled and reconstructed with small carved stones. The Fountain must have contained a second stone spout as well. Similar fountains, known locally asmugrāhā, can be found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019: 101-102). Given that a similar fountain was built in Dullu in 1568 CE (DLK0370) and that it is located near the Lamji Pañcadevala (DLK0320), which is likely to date from the 13th-15th century, it is possible to speculate that this Fountain was constructed between the 14th and 16th centuries, corresponding to the late period of the Khaśa Malla regime (12th-14th century) and the period of the succeeding Rāskoṭi dynasty.Dhārāis a Nepālī term for fountains that is commonly used in western Nepal.Mugrāhāis another vernacular term.
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
